capabilities: Fit a coordinate system to a map image from three or more control points
Display notes with coordinate frontmatter as pins on the georeferenced image
Read coordinates from note properties in several formats, including custom property names
Draw GeoJSON reference lines, including an optional Natural Earth coastline, over the fit
Expose an API for pixel/coordinate conversion, map listing, and problem reports
disambiguation: Not a basemap or GIS tool: it never warps the image, makes no map-service requests, and does no analysis beyond fitting points to pixels.
extras: Beta: must be installed by copying files into the plugins folder and is not yet in the community plugin list; the manifest notes it has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff. Makes no network requests except an explicitly confirmed download of a public-domain Natural Earth coastline. Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later.
problem: Obsidian has no way to place notes spatially on a custom picture by real-world coordinates; map plugins rely on basemap tiles instead of the user's own image.

relations.evidence: It does no GIS analysis. No buffers, overlays or topology. That is QGIS.

summary: Georeferencing tool that pins notes carrying latitude/longitude coordinates onto a map image via control points, without altering the image.
